title.narrative: Young men's and women's entrepreneurship for self employment and productivity increased

description.narrative:
In Uganda, youth unemployment remains a significant challenge, exacerbated by a rapidly growing population where 77% of the population is under 30 years old. A substantial number of new businesses are informal, with many struggling to expand due to a lack of access to skills, finance, and markets. Refugee and host communities also face unique challenges in accessing economic opportunities due to gaps in education and skills training.
The ILO's intervention focuses on empowering young men and women, particularly in refugee-hosting areas, through entrepreneurship and self-employment initiatives. By enhancing skills, access to finance, and market opportunities, the programme aims to reduce unemployment and foster sustainable enterprises. Key strategies include expanding vocational and technical training, strengthening the National Apprenticeship Framework, and supporting micro-, small-, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) with digital and green business development strategies.
The ILO collaborates with the Government of Uganda, employers' and workers' organizations, and other development partners to implement these initiatives. The expected outcomes include increased entrepreneurship and productivity, improved access to decent work for youth and refugees, and strengthened support for MSMEs. These actions align with Uganda’s National Development Plan, the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework, and key international labour standards, with a focus on gender equality, inclusivity, and the formalization of informal businesses.
This comprehensive strategy contributes to the achievement of the UN's Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 8 (decent work and economic growth) and SDG 4 (quality education).
